title: Set a proximity sensor's gap to 1.0 mm with a feeler leaf, then lock its cam clamp
instruction: Set the proximity sensor's gap to 1.0 mm with the feeler leaf, lock the clamp lever, and put the leaf back in its tray.
context: Industrial machinery mechanics, machinery maintenance workers and millwrights (about 538,300 US jobs in 2024, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook) routinely reset the face-to-target gap of an inductive sensor after a swap or a crash, with a feeler leaf and not by eye. Set too close, the first machine cycle drives the target into the sensor's face and stops the line; set too far, the sensor drops out when the slide wobbles or warms and the line stops on a false 'no part'. Here a replacement sensor has just been slid into its open clamp. The leaf has to stand upright between the face and the target while the sensor is brought up to it, the clamp is locked while the leaf is still pinched, and only then is the leaf drawn out sideways.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) A Turck BI2-M12-AP6X-H1141 inductive sensor (chrome-brass M12 x 1 barrel with a yellow face, 52 mm long with a black M12 connector (14 mm round, 12 mm long) at the rear, 31 g, rated switching distance 2 mm, secured operating distance 1.62 mm) lies along x at y 0, its axis 12.5 mm over the table, in a split clamp block (our own part, 6061 aluminium, 22 mm along x, 45 mm across, 25 mm tall, x 280 to 302 mm): a 12.2 mm bore along x on the sensor's axis, split at the axis plane into a base and a 12.5 mm cap; the cap pivots on an M6 socket screw on the +y side and is pulled down by the cam lever on the -y side; the base is screwed to the machine bed. The sensor is a slide in the open clamp: it moves along x with a light drag. Its face starts at x 306 mm. (2) A steel trip dog (24 x 24 mm, 4 mm thick) on a 40 x 40 x 34 mm carriage parked at its end stop, fixed, its face at x 318 mm: the face-to-dog gap is 12.0 mm. The gap to set is 1.00 mm (half the rated distance). (3) The clamp's cam lever, a KIPP K0006.1501406X20 (adjustable cam lever, size 1, M6 x 20 stud, A 70.4 mm, red aluminium), pivots on its cam pin along x over the block's right (-y) top edge at x 291 mm, stands open 70 degrees up; turned down flat its cam pulls the cap onto the barrel and holds the sensor where it is (the thrust piece is set so it clamps at flat). (4) A feeler leaf: 1.00 mm x 12.7 mm x 203 mm steel (silver) riveted 25 mm into an orange handle 22 mm (x) x 40 mm (y) x 24 mm tall, 30 g, lying on its edge along y in a green rack tray (60 x 270 mm outside, 8 mm tall, x 200 to 260 mm, y -380 to -110 mm) on the right, its tip at y -115 mm, x 230 mm, the handle's centre at y -313 mm. The leaf stands upright on its handle; its blade is 12.7 mm tall, so it overlaps the sensor's face (the face is 12 mm round, centred 12.5 mm up). Nothing else is on the table. The leaf's 203 mm blade lets the hand that holds its handle stay about 20 cm from the hand at the sensor's rear.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the sensor's slide, the lever's angle, the leaf's pose and both grippers. Gap: the dog's face minus the sensor's face (12.0 mm at the start, less the slide). Lever shut: within 5 degrees of its stop. Good gap: 1.00 mm within 0.25 mm. In range: 0.50 to 1.62 mm. Out of range but readable: 0.30 to 4.0 mm. Locked on the leaf: judged on the step the lever last came shut (into its last 5 degrees after being 20 degrees or more open): the leaf's blade stood upright and square (within 10 degrees) between the face and the dog, covering 6 mm or more of the face's 12 mm round, each of its two flat faces within 0.25 mm of the face it meets (the sensor's face, the dog), and the gap within 0.25 mm of the leaf's 1.00 mm. Leaf out: every point of the leaf at least 30 mm from the gap's centre line (top view). In tray: every point of the leaf over the tray's 60 x 270 mm footprint and its lowest point within 10 mm of the tray's floor. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the sensor, the lever and the leaf, and over that 1 s the slide moves under 0.2 mm, the lever under 1 degree and the leaf under 1 mm and 0.3 degrees. Score 0 if at any time the lever has been shut with the gap under 0.30 mm (the first machine cycle would drive the dog into the face), and 0 unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 lever shut, good gap, locked on the leaf, leaf out and in the tray; 0.75 the same with the leaf out but not in the tray; 0.5 lever shut with a good gap and the leaf still in the gap or not locked on it, or lever shut with the gap in range (not good) and the leaf out; 0.25 lever shut with the gap 0.30 to 4.0 mm otherwise, or a good gap with the lever open; 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: gap, go and no-go leaves for the 1.00 +- 0.25 mm window: a 0.75 mm leaf enters and a 1.25 mm leaf does not, then a 3 N pull on the sensor moves it under 0.05 mm; lever shut, a protractor (5 degrees); locked on the leaf, video of the leaf standing square in the gap, held up by the drag of both faces after the hand lets go, as the lever comes down; leaf out and in tray, a 30 mm spacer block and a look from above, a rule from the floor (10 mm); hands off, a 30 mm spacer block against each hand, 30 fps video over the last 1 s and a dial indicator on the sensor body (0.2 mm); crash, the lever shut with a 0.30 mm leaf unable to enter.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The slide is a position drive that follows the sensor each step while the lever is open (a light drag) and holds its place once shut (2 N per mm; a real clamp is stiffer). The cam lever has two notches it snaps to (open, shut): a declared over-centre rule; the cam's clamping force is not modelled. The block is our own part; the dog, carriage, handle and friction (0.6) are estimates. The sensor's jam nuts are left off; the carriage is fixed.
reset_notes: Lift the cam lever to 70 degrees and slide the sensor back until its face is 12.0 mm from the dog's face (face at x 306 mm). Put the leaf upright on its handle in the rack tray, its tip at y -115 mm, x 230 mm, the blade along y. Nothing is consumed; a real feeler leaf should be wiped and checked for a kink between trials.
